Drawings & ordering

Define the drawing revision, working surfaces, material and quantity. Review quotation scope, sample approval and the information needed to order.

How we work

Follow the LZZ order process, starting with your drawing and quotation. Agree on sample checks and production requirements before arranging shipment.

Define part requirements before machining

Prepare a machining drawing that defines the working surfaces and critical dimensions. Include material, finish and inspection requirements.

Machining guides

Choose milling, turning or multi-axis machining from the part geometry. Specify the material grade, finish and dimensions to check after treatment.

Choosing CNC milling, turning or 5-axis machining

Choose a machining process from the part geometry. Compare turning, milling and multi-axis setups, with the drawing details needed for a quotation.

Specifying material and finish for a machined part

Specify the material and finish on your CNC part drawing. Identify mating surfaces and dimensions after treatment, with the records required for acceptance.

Production & shipping

Carry the approved drawing into repeat production. Agree packing, transit, delivery terms and the documents that accompany the parts.

Planning CNC prototypes and repeat batches

Approve a prototype specification, then plan the setup and inspection for repeat batches. Confirm material, finish and order terms before increasing the quantity.

Shipping CNC parts internationally

Agree packing and delivery terms for an international CNC parts order. Check document requirements and allow transit time beyond the production schedule.
